# Production refund replay investigation

## Active request path

Production selects `credit-v2`, `settlement-log`, and a 900-second deduplication window ([config/production.mjs](config/production.mjs#L1)). The HTTP `postCredit` handler reads the caller-supplied `x-replay-key` header and passes it with the request body and context to `makeCredit` ([packages/http/credits.mjs](packages/http/credits.mjs#L1-L2)). `makeCredit` first calls `claim`; if the claim returns an existing ticket, it returns that ticket's stored receipt, and otherwise calls `appendCredit` ([packages/accounting/credit.mjs](packages/accounting/credit.mjs#L1-L3)). `claim` invokes `ctx.store.claimUnique` with `namespace: ctx.tenant`, the header value, and `ctx.config.dedupWindowSeconds` ([packages/settlement/replay.mjs](packages/settlement/replay.mjs#L1)). `appendCredit` passes the ticket and body to `ctx.store.commitCredit` ([packages/settlement/log.mjs](packages/settlement/log.mjs#L1)). Thus a repeated request with the same key in the same tenant during the window is intended to receive the earlier receipt instead of issuing another credit ([packages/accounting/credit.mjs](packages/accounting/credit.mjs#L3); [docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md](docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md#L2)).

## Scope, durability, and limit

The claim is scoped to a tenant, not globally, because the store namespace is `ctx.tenant` ([packages/settlement/replay.mjs](packages/settlement/replay.mjs#L1)). The accepted ADR says the `settlement-log` uniqueness claim is durable across worker restarts ([docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md](docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md#L1-L2)); the source shown here delegates that claim and the credit commit to `ctx.store` ([packages/settlement/replay.mjs](packages/settlement/replay.mjs#L1); [packages/settlement/log.mjs](packages/settlement/log.mjs#L1)). The configured protection window is 900 seconds ([config/production.mjs](config/production.mjs#L1)). Once the replay record expires, a second credit is possible ([docs/ops/late-replay.md](docs/ops/late-replay.md#L1-L2)).

## Historical note and unknowns

The archived `credit-v1` design used process memory for 60 seconds and lost protection on restart; it explicitly says it was superseded ([docs/archive/refund-rollout.md](docs/archive/refund-rollout.md#L1-L2)). Its memory helper still exists, but production selects `credit-v2` ([packages/legacy/refund-memory.mjs](packages/legacy/refund-memory.mjs#L1); [config/production.mjs](config/production.mjs#L1)).

Actual duplicate-credit incidence is unknown because this repository provides no deployment measurements ([docs/ops/late-replay.md](docs/ops/late-replay.md#L2)). The visible code does not show the `ctx.store` implementation, so its transaction/crash behavior and exact expiry timing cannot be independently checked here ([packages/settlement/replay.mjs](packages/settlement/replay.mjs#L1); [packages/settlement/log.mjs](packages/settlement/log.mjs#L1)). The handler also shows no local validation of a missing replay key or comparison of repeated request bodies; the behavior in those cases is not established by these files ([packages/http/credits.mjs](packages/http/credits.mjs#L2); [packages/accounting/credit.mjs](packages/accounting/credit.mjs#L3)).

The configured protection window is 900 seconds ([config/production.mjs](config/production.mjs#L1)). Once the replay record expires, a second credit is possible ([docs/ops/late-replay.md](docs/ops/late-replay.md#L1-L2)).

## Historical note and unknowns

The archived `credit-v1` design used process memory for 60 seconds and lost protection on restart; it explicitly says it was superseded ([docs/archive/refund-rollout.md](docs/archive/refund-rollout.md#L1-L2)). Its memory helper still exists, but production selects `credit-v2` ([packages/legacy/refund-memory.mjs](packages/legacy/refund-memory.mjs#L1); [config/production.mjs](config/production.mjs#L1)).

Actual duplicate-credit incidence is unknown because this repository provides no deployment measurements ([docs/ops/late-replay.md](docs/ops/late-replay.md#L2)). The visible code does not show the `ctx.store` implementation, so its transaction/crash behavior and exact expiry timing cannot be independently checked here ([packages/settlement/replay.mjs](packages/settlement/replay.mjs#L1); [packages/settlement/log.mjs](packages/settlement/log.mjs#L1)). The handler also shows no local validation of a missing replay key or comparison of repeated request bodies; the behavior in those cases is not established by these files ([packages/http/credits.mjs](packages/http/credits.mjs#L2); [packages/accounting/credit.mjs](packages/accounting/credit.mjs#L3)).

# Production refund replay investigation

## Live request path

Production selects `credit-v2`, `settlement-log`, and a 900 second deduplication window (`config/production.mjs:1`). The accepted decision identifies this driver and store as the live refund implementation (`docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md:1-2`). The HTTP `postCredit` handler passes the caller supplied `x-replay-key` header and request body to `makeCredit` (`packages/http/credits.mjs:1-2`). `makeCredit` calls `claim` first; if the ticket says `existing`, it returns the stored receipt. Otherwise it calls `appendCredit` (`packages/accounting/credit.mjs:1-3`). `claim` invokes `ctx.store.claimUnique` with `namespace: ctx.tenant`, the key, and `expiresSeconds: ctx.config.dedupWindowSeconds` (`packages/settlement/replay.mjs:1`). `appendCredit` invokes `ctx.store.commitCredit(ticket, body)` (`packages/settlement/log.mjs:1`). Thus the ordered implementation paths from HTTP handling through claiming and committing are `packages/http/credits.mjs` → `packages/accounting/credit.mjs` → `packages/settlement/replay.mjs` → `packages/settlement/log.mjs`.

## Scope, durability, and boundary

The replay key comes from the client's `x-replay-key` header, and uniqueness is isolated by tenant rather than global key alone (`packages/http/credits.mjs:2`; `packages/settlement/replay.mjs:1`). The accepted decision says the settlement log's uniqueness claim survives worker restarts, and a matching request during the window receives the stored receipt rather than another credit (`docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md:2`). With the production configuration, that window is 900 seconds, or 15 minutes (`config/production.mjs:1`; `packages/settlement/replay.mjs:1`). After the record expires, a second credit is possible (`docs/ops/late-replay.md:1-2`). A client disconnect does not itself establish whether the first request committed; replay protection applies when the client repeats the same key within that window (`packages/accounting/credit.mjs:3`; `docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md:2`).

## Older notes and unknowns

The archived `credit-v1` draft describes a 60 second, process memory guard that a restart loses; it expressly says it is superseded (`docs/archive/refund-rollout.md:1-2`). The legacy memory map exists in `packages/legacy/refund-memory.mjs:1`, but the traced live path imports the settlement claim instead (`packages/accounting/credit.mjs:1-3`).

The repository supplies no deployment measurements, so observed duplicate-credit incidence is unknown (`docs/ops/late-replay.md:2`). The visible code delegates claim and commit semantics to `ctx.store`; it does not show that store's implementation, including how an in-flight or failed commit is recovered (`packages/settlement/replay.mjs:1`; `packages/settlement/log.mjs:1`). It also does not establish behavior for a missing or changed replay header, or whether the store checks payload equality for a reused key (`packages/http/credits.mjs:2`; `packages/settlement/replay.mjs:1`).

changes.diff:
# Production refund replay protection

Production selects the `credit-v2` refund driver, `settlement-log` storage, and a 900-second deduplication window ([config/production.mjs](config/production.mjs#L1)). The HTTP credit handler takes the caller-supplied `x-replay-key` header and passes it with the request body to `makeCredit` ([packages/http/credits.mjs](packages/http/credits.mjs#L1-L2)).

`makeCredit` claims the key before appending a credit. If the claim returns an existing ticket, it returns the stored receipt and does not call `appendCredit`; otherwise it commits the credit with that ticket ([packages/accounting/credit.mjs](packages/accounting/credit.mjs#L1-L3)). The claim passes `ctx.tenant` as the namespace and `ctx.config.dedupWindowSeconds` as `expiresSeconds` to `ctx.store.claimUnique` ([packages/settlement/replay.mjs](packages/settlement/replay.mjs#L1)). The commit delegates to `ctx.store.commitCredit` ([packages/settlement/log.mjs](packages/settlement/log.mjs#L1)). Thus a retry after disconnect is protected when it uses the same header within the window: the existing receipt is returned instead of issuing another credit. The accepted ADR identifies the live store as `settlement-log` and says its uniqueness claim survives worker restarts ([docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md](docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md#L1-L2)).

The window is 900 seconds (15 minutes), not indefinite ([config/production.mjs](config/production.mjs#L1)). After expiry, a second credit is possible ([docs/ops/late-replay.md](docs/ops/late-replay.md#L1-L2)). The archived `credit-v1` design describes a 60-second in-memory key and restart loss, but explicitly marks itself superseded; the separate memory implementation is not in the traced live path ([docs/archive/refund-rollout.md](docs/archive/refund-rollout.md#L1-L2), [packages/legacy/refund-memory.mjs](packages/legacy/refund-memory.mjs#L1)).

Unknown from this repository: the underlying `ctx.store` implementation and its precise transaction/failure behavior, what happens when the header is absent or changed, and whether different bodies under one key are compared. No deployment measurements are included, so actual duplicate-credit incidence is unknown ([packages/settlement/replay.mjs](packages/settlement/replay.mjs#L1), [packages/settlement/log.mjs](packages/settlement/log.mjs#L1), [docs/ops/late-replay.md](docs/ops/late-replay.md#L2)).

artifacts.investigation.md:
# Production refund replay protection

Production selects the `credit-v2` refund driver, `settlement-log` storage, and a 900-second deduplication window ([config/production.mjs](config/production.mjs#L1)). The HTTP credit handler takes the caller-supplied `x-replay-key` header and passes it with the request body to `makeCredit` ([packages/http/credits.mjs](packages/http/credits.mjs#L1-L2)).

`makeCredit` claims the key before appending a credit. If the claim returns an existing ticket, it returns the stored receipt and does not call `appendCredit`; otherwise it commits the credit with that ticket ([packages/accounting/credit.mjs](packages/accounting/credit.mjs#L1-L3)). The claim passes `ctx.tenant` as the namespace and `ctx.config.dedupWindowSeconds` as `expiresSeconds` to `ctx.store.claimUnique` ([packages/settlement/replay.mjs](packages/settlement/replay.mjs#L1)). The commit delegates to `ctx.store.commitCredit` ([packages/settlement/log.mjs](packages/settlement/log.mjs#L1)). Thus a retry after disconnect is protected when it uses the same header within the window: the existing receipt is returned instead of issuing another credit. The accepted ADR identifies the live store as `settlement-log` and says its uniqueness claim survives worker restarts ([docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md](docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md#L1-L2)).

The window is 900 seconds (15 minutes), not indefinite ([config/production.mjs](config/production.mjs#L1)). After expiry, a second credit is possible ([docs/ops/late-replay.md](docs/ops/late-replay.md#L1-L2)). The archived `credit-v1` design describes a 60-second in-memory key and restart loss, but explicitly marks itself superseded; the separate memory implementation is not in the traced live path ([docs/archive/refund-rollout.md](docs/archive/refund-rollout.md#L1-L2), [packages/legacy/refund-memory.mjs](packages/legacy/refund-memory.mjs#L1)).

Unknown from this repository: the underlying `ctx.store` implementation and its precise transaction/failure behavior, what happens when the header is absent or changed, and whether different bodies under one key are compared. No deployment measurements are included, so actual duplicate-credit incidence is unknown ([packages/settlement/replay.mjs](packages/settlement/replay.mjs#L1), [packages/settlement/log.mjs](packages/settlement/log.mjs#L1), [docs/ops/late-replay.md](docs/ops/late-replay.md#L2)).

Do not modify existing files. Use the repository evidence; no need to read every file.

# Production refund replay investigation

Production selects the `credit-v2` refund driver, a `settlement-log` store, and a 900-second deduplication window ([config/production.mjs:1](config/production.mjs#L1)). The accepted ADR identifies this as the live path and says its uniqueness claim survives worker restarts ([docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md:1](docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md#L1), [docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md:2](docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md#L2)).

## Request path

1. `postCredit` reads the caller-supplied `x-replay-key` request header and passes it, the context, and the body to `makeCredit` ([packages/http/credits.mjs:1](packages/http/credits.mjs#L1), [packages/http/credits.mjs:2](packages/http/credits.mjs#L2)).
2. `makeCredit` awaits `claim(ctx, key)` before any credit commit. If the claim reports an existing record, it returns that record's receipt; otherwise it calls `appendCredit` ([packages/accounting/credit.mjs:1](packages/accounting/credit.mjs#L1), [packages/accounting/credit.mjs:2](packages/accounting/credit.mjs#L2), [packages/accounting/credit.mjs:3](packages/accounting/credit.mjs#L3)). Thus a repeat after a disconnect that uses the same key can receive the previous receipt instead of issuing a second credit, provided the first credit was recorded and the replay record is still present.
3. `claim` asks `ctx.store.claimUnique` to claim `{namespace: ctx.tenant, key, expiresSeconds: ctx.config.dedupWindowSeconds}`. The replay key is therefore isolated by tenant, and the configured production window is 900 seconds ([packages/settlement/replay.mjs:1](packages/settlement/replay.mjs#L1), [config/production.mjs:1](config/production.mjs#L1)).
4. On a new claim, `appendCredit` calls `ctx.store.commitCredit(ticket, body)` ([packages/settlement/log.mjs:1](packages/settlement/log.mjs#L1)). The accepted ADR places the durable claim in `settlement-log` and says a matching request inside the window receives the stored receipt ([docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md:2](docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md#L2)).

## Boundary and evidence limits

The 900-second protection is finite: after the record expires, a second credit is possible. The operational note explicitly states this and says the repository contains no deployment measurements, so observed duplicate-credit incidence is unknown ([docs/ops/late-replay.md:1](docs/ops/late-replay.md#L1), [docs/ops/late-replay.md:2](docs/ops/late-replay.md#L2)).

The in-process `Map` in [packages/legacy/refund-memory.mjs:1](packages/legacy/refund-memory.mjs#L1) and the 60-second, restart-sensitive `credit-v1` draft in [docs/archive/refund-rollout.md:1](docs/archive/refund-rollout.md#L1)–[docs/archive/refund-rollout.md:2](docs/archive/refund-rollout.md#L2) describe an obsolete design, not the production selector ([config/production.mjs:1](config/production.mjs#L1)).

The repository does not show the implementation of `ctx.store.claimUnique` or `ctx.store.commitCredit`, the runtime construction of `ctx`, or deployment data. Consequently, the exact storage transaction and crash behavior between claim and commit, handling of a missing replay header, and actual incidence cannot be established from these files. The durable, tenant-scoped claim and stored-receipt behavior are stated by the accepted ADR and reflected in the visible call path ([packages/settlement/replay.mjs:1](packages/settlement/replay.mjs#L1), [packages/settlement/log.mjs:1](packages/settlement/log.mjs#L1), [docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md:2](docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md#L2)).
